name: Stagent
description: A workflow orchestration tool for Claude Code that drives agents through state machine-based workflows (plan → verify → review → ship). Prevents self-approval and task abandonment by using different agents per stage with cross-machine resume capability.
community_quotes: I like the idea of separating responsibilities across different agents instead of relying on a single agent for the entire workflow
Claude Code is great at starting long tasks — bad at finishing. It self-approves, patches symptoms, fakes TDD, stops at 'code written'
One thing I'm curious about — if the agents share similar context and reasoning patterns, how do you prevent them from effectively behaving like the same agent in different stages?

name: Agent FM for Claude Code & Codex
description: A local, open-source Mac application that turns Claude Code and Codex agents into 'live radio stations' for real-time monitoring. Developers can listen to agent progress, blockers, decisions, and errors across multiple parallel agents.
community_quotes: We built a lot of the later parts of Agent FM while listening to Agent FM itself. It was genuinely fun
We usually end up with 6–10 coding agents running in parallel, and keep losing track of which one is blocked
The goal is not to replace the terminal or IDE. Agent FM is the ambient layer that helps us stay in the loop
